node-2.label: A white woman in her 20s with unremarkable medical and ocular history presented with decreased vision in right eye; symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation, when she was struck by lightning directly to the right forehead while hiking.

node-3.label: Initial physical examination showed uncorrected visual acuity 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS, symmetric pupils with no relative afferent pupillary defect, normal anterior segment with absence of cataract, and no apparent abnormalities on dilated fundus examination in either eye.

node-4.label: Follow-up examinations revealed central macular thickening at 2 weeks and mild posterior subcapsular cataract in the right eye at 7 weeks.

why.why: Direct lightning strike to the right forehead with symptom onset, delayed macular thickening and posterior subcapsular cataract, plus follow-up OCT showing outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption, objectively support lightning-induced ocular injury. The radiologist confirms that these structural changes are characteristic of lightning injury and refute functional visual loss or unrelated disease, so confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.95.

The initially normal examination raised the possibility of functional/non-organic visual loss, but follow-up OCT demonstrates objective structural abnormalities including outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption, along with delayed posterior subcapsular cataract. The radiologist explicitly states that these structural changes refute functional visual loss, so confidence is lowered from 0.1 to 0.02.

The clear temporal relationship between the direct lightning strike and symptom onset, together with objective structural findings on OCT and delayed posterior subcapsular cataract, strongly favors lightning-induced ocular injury. The radiologist analysis explicitly refutes unrelated ocular disease, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.01.

node-9.label: Radiologist analysis states delayed posterior subcapsular cataract is a known lightning sequel even without slit-lamp confirmation
